subject: Evidence preservation: chain of custody, regional residency, and deletion schedule
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acmehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Health SecOps <security@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up on last week's incident - evidence preservation questions

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We need to lock down a few things for our audit team and legal: specifically, (1) exactly how long Redwood will retain forensic logs and analyst notes associated with the incident, (2) whether any of those artifacts will be replicated outside the US region, and (3) the chain-of-custody process if Acme requests a sealed export for our compliance review.

Could you confirm the retention window for raw request/response logs and any derived forensic artifacts? Also let me know what the export process looks like (format, hashes, who signs off) and whether we can get a tamper-evident bundle.

Appreciate a quick confirmation so I can brief our auditors.

—Samira
Samira Khan
Security Program Manager, Acme Health
security@acmehealth.com

Attachments: incident_summary_acme_20261129.pdf (summary provided by Acme)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up on last week's incident - evidence preservation questions

Samira — thanks for raising this. High level answers below; I'll loop in Legal for the chain-of-custody signoff.

1) Retention windows: by default we retain raw request/response logs associated with customer API keys for 90 days; aggregated diagnostic logs (sampling, metrics) are retained for 365 days. For post-incident forensic snapshots (manual captures taken by our IR team) we can hold those for up to 12 months on request and mark them as "forensic_evidence" to prevent normal deletion policies from applying.

2) Residency: your customer data and associated raw logs remain in the region you signed up for (us-west). For the forensic snapshots we create, the copies are kept in the same US region unless the customer requests cross-region transfer. We do not replicate forensic bundles to EU/APAC by default.

3) Export and chain-of-custody: we can produce an export bundle (tar.gz) that includes logs (gz), a manifest of files, SHA-256 hashes, and an export certificate signed by Redwood incident lead. If Acme needs an evidence-sealed export, Legal and IR will coordinate a signed chain-of-custody form and an audit trail showing who accessed/created the bundle and when. Typical signatories: Redwood Incident Lead + Acme SecOps lead.

I'll attach a sample chain_of_custody_template and propose a timeline — draft bundle produced within 5 business days of request, notarized/co-signed within 10 business days if required. Marissa / Karthik, can Legal confirm the wording and any constraints on handing over raw PII-containing artifacts?

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Security Partnerships | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Attachments: chain_of_custody_template.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:36:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up on last week's incident - evidence preservation questions

Samira / Jonas — quick legal note from my side. We can produce a curated forensic bundle but need to minimize transfer of any customer PII unless Acme's DPA and access controls are in place. If the export contains user-level request/response payloads with PHI, we'll require an executed data transfer addendum that explicitly permits the transfer and specifies retention/deletion expectations for the delivered bundle.

Proposed changes to the timeline Jonas suggested:
- Draft forensic bundle (with redaction options): 3 business days to produce a redacted draft; 5 business days for full raw export if DPA in place.
- Chain-of-custody form: we will sign on Redwood's side; Acme's signoff will finalize the sealed handoff window.

Mina, please confirm whether Redwood's standard DTA covers transfers of PHI in sealed forensic exports; if not, we should flag this as a procurement/legal step and keep the draft bundle redacted. Samira, if you can provide the auditor contact and documented purpose for the export (audit vs court), that will guide redaction level.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachment referenced: incident_summary_acme_20261129.pdf (viewed)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up on last week's incident - evidence preservation questions

Adding operational details from IR:

- Forensic capture contents: process logs (request IDs, timestamps), worker/kernel-level traces (when applicable), and a snapshot of relevant model-serving KV caches if they were in-scope for the incident. We include a manifest and SHA-256 checksums for every file.
- Tamper-evidence: we can provide both signed manifest and a PGP-signed checksum file. If Acme requires a physical notarized seal, we will coordinate with Legal but note this extends timelines.
- Access logs: we will include an access audit (who downloaded/created the bundle) and retention metadata. These access logs are kept for 2 years by default for internal audit; we can include the segment relevant to this incident in the export.

Operational ask for Acme: please tell us the minimum set of artifacts you need (e.g., only control-plane logs + request IDs vs full payloads). If you only need metadata and hashes for audit, we can redact payloads and deliver much faster.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Security Engineering Manager, Incident Response | Redwood Inference

Attachment: requested_log_indexes.txt (list of log indexes we expect to pull)

Thanks — that's very helpful. Acme's auditors want: (A) a sealed bundle with request and response headers (we can redact bodies with PHI), (B) the manifest + SHA-256 file, and (C) an access audit for the 30 days around the incident. We have an executed DPA that allows transfers for audit purposes but I will attach a signed DTA for sealed exports tomorrow.

Can we proceed with the redacted draft first (3 business days) and we will fast-track the DTA so you can do the full raw export if needed? Also Sam quick question to Redwood team: will the redacted draft still include the KV cache snapshot if relevant, or do you treat that as a payload item that requires the full DTA?

Appreciate the responsiveness — if you can confirm the 3-day draft and the 5-day raw timeline once DTA signed, we can align with auditors.

—Samira
